blocks.en: A Word Before We Begin
blocks.es_reference: Una Palabra Antes de Comenzar

blocks.en: This course examines groups whose teaching departs from the gospel of Jesus Christ — some that call themselves Christian, and some that belong to the great religions of the world. Its method is simple, and it will not change: we take each group's teaching as it actually is, and we test it by the Word of God, and where it departs from the gospel we say so plainly. That is not unkindness; it is the one thing love truly requires, for every person we study is made in God's image and is someone for whom Christ died, and the most loving thing we can do for anyone is to tell them the truth about Christ. So we set our course by a single verse, and need not repeat the sentiment in every unit that follows: we speak "the truth in love" (Ephesians 4:15) — all the truth, and in love. What remains is to learn what a cult actually is, and how to tell one.
blocks.es_reference: Este curso examina grupos cuya enseñanza se aparta del evangelio de Jesucristo — algunos que se llaman cristianos, y algunos que pertenecen a las grandes religiones del mundo. Su método es sencillo, y no cambiará: tomamos la enseñanza de cada grupo tal como realmente es, y la probamos por la Palabra de Dios, y donde se aparta del evangelio lo decimos con claridad. Eso no es falta de bondad; es lo único que el amor verdaderamente requiere, pues cada persona que estudiamos está hecha a imagen de Dios y es alguien por quien Cristo murió, y lo más bondadoso que podemos hacer por cualquiera es decirle la verdad acerca de Cristo. Así que fijamos nuestro rumbo por un solo versículo, y no necesitamos repetir el sentimiento en cada unidad que sigue: hablamos "la verdad en amor" (Efesios 4:15) — toda la verdad, y en amor. Lo que queda es aprender qué es realmente una secta, y cómo reconocerla.

blocks.en: What Do We Mean by "Cult"?
blocks.es_reference: ¿Qué Queremos Decir con "Secta"?

blocks.en: The word "cult" is easily misused, so we must define it with care. In this course a cult is a group that claims to hold the truth about God — often claiming to be the true form of Christianity — yet denies one or more essentials of the biblical gospel, especially who Jesus Christ is and how a person is saved. A cult is not simply a group we dislike, and the word is not an insult hurled at people. It is a careful description of a teaching's relationship to the gospel.
blocks.es_reference: La palabra "secta" se usa mal con facilidad, así que debemos definirla con cuidado. En este curso, una secta es un grupo que afirma poseer la verdad acerca de Dios — a menudo afirmando ser la forma verdadera del cristianismo — pero niega uno o más elementos esenciales del evangelio bíblico, especialmente quién es Jesucristo y cómo es salva una persona. Una secta no es simplemente un grupo que nos desagrada, y la palabra no es un insulto lanzado contra las personas. Es una descripción cuidadosa de la relación de una enseñanza con el evangelio.

blocks.en: We must keep three things distinct. A cult claims Christ but denies an essential of the faith — as we will see with the Jehovah's Witnesses and the Latter-day Saints. A world religion, such as Islam, Hinduism, or Buddhism, is a wholly separate faith that does not claim to be Christianity at all. And a Christian tradition — a genuine denomination — agrees on the essentials (the Trinity, the full deity of Christ, salvation by grace through faith) while differing on secondary matters such as the mode of baptism or the form of church government. Those who agree on the gospel but differ on lesser things are brothers, not a cult. To confuse these three is to be unfair to some and careless with others.
blocks.es_reference: Debemos mantener tres cosas distintas. Una secta afirma a Cristo pero niega un elemento esencial de la fe — como veremos con los Testigos de Jehová y los Santos de los Últimos Días. Una religión del mundo, como el islam, el hinduismo o el budismo, es una fe totalmente separada que no afirma ser cristianismo en absoluto. Y una tradición cristiana — una denominación genuina — concuerda en lo esencial (la Trinidad, la plena deidad de Cristo, la salvación por gracia mediante la fe) mientras difiere en asuntos secundarios como el modo del bautismo o la forma del gobierno de la iglesia. Los que concuerdan en el evangelio pero difieren en cosas menores son hermanos, no una secta. Confundir estas tres cosas es ser injusto con unos y descuidado con otros.

blocks.en: The Marks of a Cult
blocks.es_reference: Las Marcas de una Secta

blocks.en: Cults differ from one another, and no single group shows every mark. But certain features appear again and again, and learning to recognize them helps us test wisely. The first and gravest is a different Christ: the group denies His full deity, or His true humanity, and gives us a Jesus who is less than the eternal Son of God. The second is a different gospel: salvation is made to rest, in whole or in part, on works and performance rather than on the grace of God received by faith. A third is an added authority: a new book, a living prophet, or an organization is placed alongside or above the Scriptures. Often there follows an exclusive claim — that only this group is saved — and with it a measure of control, so that to leave the group is made to feel like leaving God. Behind all of these lies a single pattern: something has been added to, or taken from, the finished work of Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Las sectas difieren entre sí, y ningún grupo muestra todas las marcas. Pero ciertos rasgos aparecen una y otra vez, y aprender a reconocerlos nos ayuda a probar con sabiduría. La primera y más grave es un Cristo diferente: el grupo niega su plena deidad, o su verdadera humanidad, y nos da un Jesús que es menos que el eterno Hijo de Dios. La segunda es un evangelio diferente: la salvación se hace descansar, en todo o en parte, sobre las obras y el desempeño en lugar de sobre la gracia de Dios recibida por la fe. Una tercera es una autoridad añadida: un libro nuevo, un profeta viviente, o una organización se coloca junto a las Escrituras o por encima de ellas. A menudo sigue una pretensión exclusiva — que solo este grupo es salvo — y con ella cierto control, de modo que dejar el grupo se hace sentir como dejar a Dios. Detrás de todo esto hay un solo patrón: algo se ha añadido, o se ha quitado, a la obra consumada de Cristo.

blocks.en: The Biblical Tests
blocks.es_reference: Las Pruebas Bíblicas

blocks.en: We do not test these groups by our own opinions, but by Scripture, which teaches us plainly how to test. Paul writes that if anyone preaches "any other gospel" than the true one, even "an angel from heaven," he is to be accursed (Galatians 1:6-9): the gospel of grace may not be added to or subtracted from. He warns the Corinthians that a deceiver comes preaching "another Jesus," "a different spirit," and "a different gospel" (2 Corinthians 11:3-4) — a counterfeit can look very much like the real thing. John commands us not to "believe every spirit, but test the spirits" (1 John 4:1), and the test he gives centers on Christ: whether one confesses that "Jesus Christ has come in the flesh" (1 John 4:2), truly God and truly man. And Jude urges us to "contend earnestly for the faith which was once for all delivered to the saints" (Jude 3) — there is a fixed apostolic gospel, and later "revelations" that change it are to be rejected.
blocks.es_reference: No probamos a estos grupos por nuestras propias opiniones, sino por la Escritura, que nos enseña claramente cómo probar. Pablo escribe que si alguno predica "otro evangelio" diferente del verdadero, aunque sea "un ángel del cielo", sea anatema (Gálatas 1:6-9): al evangelio de la gracia no se le puede añadir ni quitar. Advierte a los corintios que un engañador viene predicando "otro Jesús", "otro espíritu" y "otro evangelio" (2 Corintios 11:3-4) — una falsificación puede parecerse mucho a lo verdadero. Juan nos manda no "creáis a todo espíritu, sino probad los espíritus" (1 Juan 4:1), y la prueba que da se centra en Cristo: si uno confiesa que "Jesucristo ha venido en carne" (1 Juan 4:2), verdaderamente Dios y verdaderamente hombre. Y Judas nos exhorta a "contender ardientemente por la fe que ha sido una vez dada a los santos" (Judas 3) — hay un evangelio apostólico fijo, y las "revelaciones" posteriores que lo cambian han de ser rechazadas.

blocks.en: All of these come down to two questions we will call the root-test, for the whole tree of faith grows from them. First: Who is Jesus? Is He the eternal God the Son, truly God and truly man? Second: How is a person saved? By grace alone, through faith alone, in Christ alone — or by works? Get these two right, and the tree is sound; get either one wrong at the root, and it is another tree and another gospel, however much of the bark may look the same.
blocks.es_reference: Todo esto se reduce a dos preguntas que llamaremos la prueba de la raíz, pues todo el árbol de la fe crece de ellas. Primera: ¿Quién es Jesús? ¿Es el eterno Dios el Hijo, verdaderamente Dios y verdaderamente hombre? Segunda: ¿Cómo es salva una persona? ¿Por gracia sola, mediante la fe sola, en Cristo solo — o por obras? Acierte en estas dos, y el árbol es sano; yerre en cualquiera de las dos en la raíz, y es otro árbol y otro evangelio, por mucho que la corteza parezca la misma.

blocks.en: How We Will Study Them
blocks.es_reference: Cómo los Estudiaremos

blocks.en: Our method in every unit will be the same, and it is a method of both honesty and love. First, we will state each group's beliefs fairly, in their own words and from their own sources, not from caricatures or rumors. This is simply the Golden Rule applied to disagreement: we describe others as we would want to be described. Second, we will test the root by Scripture — asking the two questions and letting the Word of God render the verdict. Third, we will aim at the person redemptively. When Paul stood among the idols and philosophers of Athens, he did not simply denounce them; he reasoned with them, quoted their own poets, and pointed them to the risen Christ (Acts 17:22-31). That is our aim too: not merely to refute an error, but to win a person.
blocks.es_reference: Nuestro método en cada unidad será el mismo, y es un método de honestidad y de amor a la vez. Primero, expondremos las creencias de cada grupo justamente, en sus propias palabras y desde sus propias fuentes, no desde caricaturas ni rumores. Esto es sencillamente la Regla de Oro aplicada al desacuerdo: describimos a otros como quisiéramos ser descritos. Segundo, probaremos la raíz por la Escritura — haciendo las dos preguntas y dejando que la Palabra de Dios dé el veredicto. Tercero, apuntaremos a la persona de manera redentora. Cuando Pablo estuvo entre los ídolos y los filósofos de Atenas, no se limitó a denunciarlos; razonó con ellos, citó a sus propios poetas, y los señaló al Cristo resucitado (Hechos 17:22-31). Ese es también nuestro fin: no meramente refutar un error, sino ganar a una persona.

blocks.en: A Redemptive Aim
blocks.es_reference: Un Fin Redentor

blocks.en: So this is not a course in suspicion, and still less in pride. If we come to it looking down on others, we have already failed. The same grace that found us is the grace we long for them to find. Many who are caught in cults are sincere, moral, and devout — often more zealous than we are — and many who follow the world's religions are seeking God as best they know how. Our task is twofold, and we must hold both parts together: to hold fast the true gospel without compromise, and to reach out to every person with genuine love. We mark the error precisely so that we may reclaim the people. As we begin, let us fix our aim on that goal: to know the truth, to speak it in love, and to see men and women brought home to the true and living Christ.
blocks.es_reference: Así que este no es un curso de sospecha, y mucho menos de orgullo. Si venimos a él menospreciando a otros, ya hemos fracasado. La misma gracia que nos halló es la gracia que anhelamos que ellos hallen. Muchos de los que están atrapados en sectas son sinceros, morales y devotos — a menudo más celosos que nosotros — y muchos de los que siguen las religiones del mundo buscan a Dios lo mejor que saben. Nuestra tarea es doble, y debemos sostener ambas partes juntas: sostener firmemente el verdadero evangelio sin transigir, y acercarnos a cada persona con amor genuino. Marcamos el error precisamente para poder recuperar a las personas. Al comenzar, fijemos nuestro fin en esa meta: conocer la verdad, hablarla en amor, y ver a hombres y mujeres traídos a casa al Cristo verdadero y vivo.

mc.stem: In this course, the word 'cult' is used to describe:
options: A group claiming Christian or biblical truth that denies an essential of the gospel (especially who Christ is and how we are saved)
A group that simply worships in a different style
Any non-Christian religion in the world
mc.why: A cult claims the truth about God yet denies an essential of the gospel — above all, who Christ is and how a person is saved.

mc.stem: Which best distinguishes a 'world religion' from a 'cult' as defined here?
options: A world religion is a wholly separate faith (such as Islam or Hinduism), not a claimed form of Christianity
A world religion is always older than a cult
There is no real difference between them
A world religion simply has more members
mc.why: A world religion does not claim to be Christianity at all; a cult claims Christ while denying an essential.

mc.stem: A group that affirms the Trinity, the full deity of Christ, and salvation by grace, but differs on the mode of baptism, is best regarded as:
options: A Christian tradition — brothers, not a cult
mc.why: Agreement on the essentials makes such a group brothers who differ on secondary matters, not a cult.

mc.stem: In this course, calling a teaching a 'cult' is meant to be:
options: A personal insult against its members
A claim that its members are wicked people
A careful description of the teaching's relationship to the gospel
mc.why: The term describes how a teaching relates to the gospel; it is not an insult aimed at people.

mc.stem: The two 'root' questions that decide everything are:
options: Which holidays and which hymns the group keeps
How old the group is and how large
Who Jesus is, and how a person is saved
Which Bible translation and which prayers it uses
mc.why: The root-test asks who Christ is and how salvation comes; these two decide whether the gospel stands.

mc.stem: Galatians 1:8 warns that if anyone — even an angel from heaven — preaches another gospel, he is:
options: To be admired for his zeal
mc.why: Paul pronounces a curse on any other gospel, even one preached by an angel — the gospel may not be changed.

mc.stem: In 2 Corinthians 11:3-4, Paul warns that a deceiver may bring:
options: Another Jesus, a different spirit, and a different gospel
mc.why: Paul warns of a counterfeit — another Jesus, another spirit, another gospel — that can look like the real thing.

mc.stem: According to 1 John 4:1-3, believers are told to:
options: Test the spirits, whether they are of God
mc.why: John commands us not to believe every spirit, but to test the spirits by the truth about Christ.

mc.stem: The test John gives in 1 John 4 centers on the confession that:
options: Jesus was a good moral teacher
Jesus is one prophet among many
Jesus Christ has come in the flesh — true God and true man
Jesus existed only as a spirit
mc.why: The test is whether one confesses that Jesus Christ has truly come in the flesh — genuinely God and man.

mc.stem: Jude 3 calls believers to contend for 'the faith once for all delivered,' which teaches that:
options: The gospel keeps changing with each age
New revelations may replace the apostolic gospel
There is a fixed apostolic gospel that must not be altered
Every generation needs a new gospel
mc.why: Jude teaches that the gospel was delivered once for all; later 'revelations' that change it are to be rejected.

mc.stem: A common mark of a cult is 'a different Christ,' meaning it:
options: Denies His full deity or His true humanity
Meets on a different day of the week
Uses a different kind of building
mc.why: A different Christ denies either His full deity or His true humanity, giving a Jesus less than the eternal Son.

mc.stem: Another common mark is 'a different gospel,' meaning salvation is made to rest on:
options: Works and performance added to grace
mc.why: A different gospel adds works and performance to grace, so salvation no longer rests on Christ alone.

mc.stem: A frequent mark of a cult is 'an added authority,' such as:
options: A new book, prophet, or organization placed alongside or above the Bible
mc.why: An added authority sets a new book, prophet, or organization beside or above the Scriptures.

mc.stem: When we study each group, we will first state its beliefs:
options: Fairly, from the group's own sources
mc.why: We state each group's beliefs fairly, from their own sources — never from caricatures.

mc.stem: Stating a group's beliefs fairly, from its own sources, is an application of:
options: The Golden Rule applied to disagreement
mc.why: Describing others as we would want to be described is the Golden Rule applied to disagreement.

mc.stem: Our aim toward the members of these groups is:
options: Redemptive — to win them to the true Christ
mc.why: The aim is not merely to refute an error but to win the person to the true Christ.

mc.stem: Ephesians 4:15 calls us to speak:
mc.why: We are to speak the truth in love — holding both together, not one without the other.

mc.stem: First Peter 3:15 says to give a reason for our hope with:
mc.why: We give the reason for our hope with meekness and respect, never with harshness.

mc.stem: Paul's engagement with the philosophers in Athens (Acts 17) models:
options: Thoughtful, respectful witness that points to the risen Christ
mc.why: In Athens Paul reasoned respectfully, even citing their poets, and pointed them to the risen Christ.

mc.stem: The overall posture of this course toward people in cults and other religions is:
options: Firm truth held together with genuine love
mc.why: We hold the true gospel firmly and reach out to every person with genuine love — truth and love together.

sa.prompt: Define what this course means by a 'cult,' and explain how it differs from a world religion.
sa.model: In this course a cult is a group that claims to hold the truth about God, often claiming to be true Christianity, yet denies an essential of the biblical gospel, especially who Christ is and how a person is saved. It is not merely a group we dislike, but a teaching that departs from the gospel at an essential point. A world religion is different: it is a wholly separate faith, such as Islam or Hinduism, that does not claim to be Christianity at all. So a cult claims Christ while denying an essential, whereas a world religion stands outside the Christian claim entirely.

sa.prompt: Explain the difference between a cult and a Christian tradition (denomination), and why differing on baptism is not the same as denying the gospel.
sa.model: A Christian tradition, or denomination, agrees with us on the essentials of the faith: the Trinity, the full deity of Christ, and salvation by grace through faith. It differs only on secondary matters, such as the mode of baptism or the form of church government. A cult, by contrast, denies one of those essentials. This is why differing over baptism is not the same as denying the gospel: baptism is a real and important question, but it is a secondary one, and those who hold the same gospel while differing on it are brothers, not a cult. To treat a fellow believer who differs on baptism as though he denied Christ would be both unfair and untrue.

sa.prompt: State the two 'root' questions and explain why they decide whether a group holds the true gospel.
sa.model: The two root questions are these: first, Who is Jesus? Is he the eternal God the Son, truly God and truly man? Second, How is a person saved? By grace alone, through faith alone, in Christ alone, or by works? They are called root questions because the whole tree of faith grows from them. If a group answers rightly about the deity of Christ and about salvation by grace through faith, the root is sound and the gospel stands. But if it gets either one wrong, denying the deity of Christ or adding works to grace, then it is a different root, and a different root makes a different tree, however similar the branches may appear.

sa.prompt: From Galatians 1:6-9, explain what makes a message 'another gospel' and the force of 'even an angel from heaven.'
sa.model: A message becomes another gospel when it changes the true gospel of grace, whether by adding to it or taking from it. Paul says that even if he himself, or an angel from heaven, should preach any other gospel than the one already preached, let him be accursed. The force of even an angel from heaven is to show that no messenger, however exalted, and no human teacher, however sincere, has the right to alter the gospel. The authority of the message does not rest on the impressiveness of the messenger but on its faithfulness to what God has revealed. So any teaching that perverts the gospel at its root, changing who Christ is or how we are saved, falls under this solemn curse, no matter who brings it.

sa.prompt: From 1 John 4:1-3, explain the test of the spirits and what confession it centers on.
sa.model: John tells us not to believe every spirit, but to test the spirits to see whether they are of God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world. The test he gives is not sincerity or success, but a confession about Christ. Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God, and every spirit that does not confess this is not of God. So the test centers on the true Christ: whether one confesses him as genuinely come in the flesh, truly God and truly man. This is why the person of Christ is the first thing we examine in any teaching, for the truth about him is the dividing line between what is of God and what is not.

sa.prompt: Name several marks of a cult and explain how they relate to the gospel.
sa.model: Cults show certain marks again and again, though not every group shows all of them. The first is a different Christ, denying his full deity or true humanity. The second is a different gospel, resting salvation on works and performance rather than on grace received by faith. A third is an added authority, placing a new book, prophet, or organization alongside or above the Scriptures. Often there is an exclusive claim, that only this group is saved, and a measure of control, so that leaving the group feels like leaving God. Each mark relates to the gospel in the same way: something has been added to, or taken from, the finished work of Christ, so that the true gospel of grace is compromised at its root.

sa.prompt: Explain the three-step method this course uses to study each group.
sa.model: The method has three steps, joining honesty and love. First, we state each group's beliefs fairly, in their own words and from their own sources, not from caricatures. This is the Golden Rule applied to disagreement. Second, we test the root by Scripture, asking the two questions about Christ and salvation and letting the Word of God give the verdict. Third, we aim at the person redemptively, following Paul in Athens, who reasoned respectfully and pointed people to the risen Christ. So we do not merely refute an error; we seek to win a person, holding the true gospel firmly while treating every individual with genuine love and respect.

sa.prompt: Explain why we must speak 'the truth in love' and with 'gentleness and respect' toward people in cults and other religions.
sa.model: We speak the truth in love because both are commanded and neither may be dropped. Truth without love becomes harsh and drives people away; love without truth becomes flattery and leaves them in error. Peter says to give a reason for our hope with gentleness and respect, and Paul says to speak the truth in love. Every person in a cult or another religion is made in the image of God and is someone for whom Christ died, so they deserve kindness, patience, and honest respect. In fact, real love is what compels us to tell them the truth rather than to leave them comfortable in a false gospel. So our witness must always join a firm holding of the truth with genuine, respectful love for the person.

sa.prompt: Using Acts 17 (Paul in Athens), describe the posture we should take toward people of other faiths.
sa.model: In Athens Paul gives us a model for meeting people of other faiths. He was grieved by their idols, yet he did not simply denounce them. He reasoned with them in the synagogue and the marketplace, he observed their altars and even quoted their own poets, and he used what he found as a bridge to the truth. Then he pointed them clearly to the living God and to the risen Christ, calling all people everywhere to repent. So our posture is neither to mock nor to stay silent, but to engage thoughtfully and with respect, listening and reasoning, and always aiming our witness at the person, that we might point them to the risen Christ.

sa.prompt: Summarize Unit 1: what a cult is, the biblical tests for discerning one, and the redemptive aim of the course.
sa.model: Unit 1 lays the foundation for the whole course. A cult is a group that claims the truth about God, often claiming to be Christian, yet denies an essential of the gospel, especially who Christ is and how a person is saved; it differs from a world religion, which is a separate faith, and from a Christian tradition, which agrees on the essentials. Scripture teaches us to test such teaching: Paul warns of another gospel and another Jesus, John tells us to test the spirits by the confession of Christ, and Jude bids us contend for the faith once delivered. It all comes down to two root questions, about the person of Christ and about salvation by grace. And the aim of the course is redemptive: to hold the true gospel firmly and to reach every person with genuine love, marking the error in order to reclaim the people for the true and living Christ.
